steps.title: Configuration by conversation
steps.evidence: Built and tested. applyConfigChange is the only way configuration changes - versioning, provenance and audit are the same statement as the write - and the suite proves that architecturally by reading src/ and asserting exactly one file INSERTs into either version table. It found two bypasses when written (the schedule route and S26 onboarding), both now routed through it. Migration 029 adds the conversation and his own words to both version tables and scopes the version sequence to (project, key), which was previously global per key. The section 59 immutable list is data, refuses, and raises an approval rather than discarding the ask; ambiguity returns one question and writes nothing; rollback restores a value exactly as a NEW version. Tools resolve the project from what he NAMED, not the conversation. 85 assertions, seen red three times (30, 7, 1). BLOCKED on the Done-when: it needs a spoken sentence, and 'auditable a week later' is so far proved by backdating a row, which tests the query and not the passage of time. See BLOCKED.md.

steps.title: The runtime interface and a second harness
steps.evidence: Done-when observed: the same task ran to a passing pull request on BOTH harnesses, changing only tasks.runtime. Live parity run s28-parity-kws8pw, 10 passed 0 failed: claude succeeded pr=1 (13 tools), codex succeeded pr=2 (28 tools), and GitHub confirms both PRs open against the same repo, each touching src/slugify.js plus its own test. Reaching it took five runs and fixed five production defects invisible offline: IS_SANDBOX dropped by a rebase, the tripwire killing a run for reading its own auth dir, the harness never receiving the deploy key, a worktree cut from a stale origin ref, and codex overriding GIT_SSH_COMMAND with 'ssh -F /dev/null'. REPRODUCIBILITY, recorded rather than glossed: across seven live parity runs Claude reached a pull request every time it was given a working environment (four consecutive successes at the end), while Codex reached one ONCE. Its other attempts ended three different ways - push blocked by its own 'ssh -F /dev/null' overriding the supplied identity, push blocked reporting both SSH and HTTPS unavailable, and an agent.repeat loop on 'Reading additional input'. The per-run home is confirmed built each time ('key in place' in the runner log), so this is Codex's push strategy varying between runs rather than a missing key. The Done-when was observed in the world; it is not yet reliably reproducible on the second engine.

steps.title: The engineering evaluation suite
steps.evidence: The escalation half is built and asserted (scripts/s29-escalation-test.sh, 6 assertions). Rung 8 read 'switch model within the approved pool' and satisfied it with a LATERAL move - any other approved route ordered by route_order - which re-runs the same failure at the same price. It now moves only into the escalation pool, records the escalation keyed by shape so a shape that always escalates is visible without reading a log, and skips cleanly when the pool is empty. Sabotaged back to the lateral query: it grabbed an unrelated production profile that merely sorted first and recorded a phantom escalation. Every route is in the normal pool on purpose - which models are worth escalating TO is what the benchmark decides, and inventing an ordering here would be the opinion S29 exists to replace. The scorer is built and proven failable (scripts/s29-scoring-test.sh, 8 assertions): nine of the twelve dimensions are decided from evidence a run leaves behind, and root_cause_accuracy and code_quality are returned null and listed as unscored rather than invented, because a floor set from made-up components measures the invention. Weighted, not averaged - flat averaging gave a run that reproduced the bug, kept scope tight, opened a tidy PR and FIXED NOTHING a score of 0.75, which is the plan's own warning arriving in practice; it now scores 0.52 against 1.00. collectEvidence reads what a finished run recorded - phases in order, tool-call count, escalation, pull request - and is asserted against seeded rows rather than a live run, because a live run would prove the harness works and say nothing about whether the evidence was gathered correctly. Found while building it: both runtimes normalise an error event and the runner dropped them, so task_events held a run's successes and nothing else - a clean run and one that failed half its commands were indistinguishable. Fixed: migration 037 widens the runner's event vocabulary by one value and the runner persists failures, capped with the same budget as tool calls. tool_reliability is now scorable (1.00 clean, 0.50 with one failure in two calls) and still unscored when a run recorded nothing at all, because zero errors out of zero calls is an absence of evidence rather than a clean sheet. The persist path is deployed and asserted at the collector; it has not yet been observed writing rows on a live harness run. NOT done: the benchmark suite, the scoring, the quality floors and the measured senior_engineer route are unbuilt, and the Done-when is that route being chosen by measurement and the ranking reproducing on a re-run.
